ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions list. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for any politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined by FATF, including domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates. The screening must be conducted at onboarding, on a continuous basis (at least daily), and upon any trigger event. The compliance team must document all screening results, maintain audit trails, and escalate any positive hits to the AML Compliance Officer within 24 hours. For Taiwan-specific risks, additional screening against the Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission's sanctions list and the Taiwan Ministry of Justice's AML/CFT database is mandatory. The protocol must also incorporate risk-based transaction monitoring for the PE buyout SPV, including wire transfers via SWIFT and syndicated loan rails, with thresholds set at USD 10,000 for cash transactions and USD 50,000 for wire transfers. All findings must be reported to the competent authorities as per PBOC Order No. 3 and Taiwan's Money Laundering Control Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Company and Commerce Registration Information System (CCRIS) of the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Traditional Chinese characters. An English name may be registered as a secondary name, but the Chinese name is the legal name. The name must follow a four-tier structure: (1) trade name (e.g., 'Sino-Foreign'), (2) business type (e.g., 'Equity Joint Venture'), (3) organization type (e.g., 'Limited Company'), and (4) additional distinguishing features (e.g., 'Private Equity Buyout SPV'). Phonetic transliteration from Chinese to English is permitted but must be consistent with the registered Chinese name. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered company name in Taiwan. The use of English names is subject to MOEA approval and must not contain prohibited tokens.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), as amended, Articles 5, 6, 7, 18, 19, 20, 27, 129, 130, 156, 161, 162, 172, 174, 175, 192, 193, 195, 201, 202, 203, 208, 228, 229, 387, 393, 399; Foreign Investment Act, Articles 4, 8 and 12; Regulations on Application Approval of Foreign Investment; Taiwan Central Bank Foreign Exchange Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan, through the One-Stop Company Registration portal; foreign investment applications are co-processed by the Investment Commission, MOEA.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration (Company Registration Application Form) together with the Articles of Incorporation and verified corporate acts.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is imposed by the Taiwan Company Act, and no blocked escrow account is mandated for a private equity buyout SPV. The paid-up capital must be subscribed in the Articles of Incorporation and remitted to a bank account opened in Taiwan. A certified public accountant capital verification report is required when paid-in capital exceeds NT$5 million or when the registry expressly requires verification. Foreign-currency capital contributions from offshore shareholders must be routed through a Taiwan foreign-exchange bank and reported to the Taiwan Central Bank for subsequent remittance freedom in respect of dividends, loan repayments, or share disposals.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF CN_JV_LTD. At the first meeting of the board of directors of CN_JV_LTD, lawfully convened on the date set forth in the notice, with all directors present and waiving further notice, the board unanimously adopted the following resolutions. RESOLVED, that the incorporation of CN_JV_LTD and the allotment and issuance of the authorized ordinary shares to the subscribers named in the register of shareholders be, and each of the same hereby is, ratified and confirmed in all respects; that the directors be, and they hereby are, authorized to issue, sign, and deliver share certificates in accordance with Article 161 of the Taiwan Company Act; and that the Chairperson take all steps needed to collect the subscribed paid-up capital, obtain the certified public accountant capital verification report, and perfect the shareholders register and share subscription ledger. RESOLVED, that the Chairperson and the General Manager are, and each of them hereby is, authorized, either singly or jointly as provided in the bank signatory card, to open, operate, designate, and close corporate, escrow, syndicated loan, securities, foreign-exchange, and payment accounts with any bank selected for CN_JV_LTD, to execute account applications, wire transfer instructions, SWIFT messages, syndicated loan documents, security agreements, pledge forms, and all ancillary bank and custodian instructions, and to appoint any third-party banking agent considered advisable for the private equity acquisition program. RESOLVED, that the registered office of CN_JV_LTD be, and it hereby is, fixed at the address of the registered agent in Taiwan as filed with the competent registry, and that the company seal, corporate minute book, shareholders register, directors register, and statutory books be kept at such registered office. RESOLVED, that the following statutory officers are, and each of them hereby is, appointed: the Chairperson, the General Manager, the Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, and the Principal Accounting Officer, each with full authority to execute and deliver corporate instruments, make regulatory filings, and direct professional advisers within their respective functions. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Chairperson and General Manager are jointly and severally authorized to obtain tax, labor, health, foreign-exchange, and any required financial services registrations, to engage independent accounting and legal counsel, to open all regulatory interfaces, to represent the company before government agencies, and to perform all acts reasonably necessary to give full force and effect to this resolution. This resolution is effective immediately upon filing the incorporation registration and shall be filed with the corporate secretary and distributed to each director.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation, Investment Qualification and Corporate Structure Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA One-Stop Company Name Registry and Investment Commission, MOEA (for non-Taiwan shareholders; special review applies to investors from regulated jurisdictions)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the MOEA company name database for identical or deceptively similar names; file online name reservation for the English and romanized name CN_JV_LTD and any Chinese style name. Submit a foreign investment pre-application to the Investment Commission, MOEA, describing the SPV private equity buyout purpose, source of funds, financing syndicate, and ultimate beneficial ownership. Include the draft Articles of Incorporation and investment plan. Await pre-screening result, especially if any mainland area investor exceeds regulatory ownership thresholds; obtain a written investment approval or no-objection letter before filing formal registration.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity cards of shareholders and directors
Detailed investment plan and proof of source of funds
Financing commitment letter or syndicated loan term sheet
Power of attorney for formation counsel if used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit two alternative names and reserve the first available; if the Investment Commission queries the foreign investment application, file a written supplemental brief within 14 days, provide bank referral letters, proof of fund origin, and expand the ultimate beneficial ownership disclosure; if approval is withheld, restructure the shareholding or investment conditions and file an administrative appeal under the Administrative Appeal Act within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders and shareholders; Taiwan notary public where required; Taiwan branch bank for capital subscription; certified public accountant licensed in Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the founding subscribers meeting, adopt the Articles of Incorporation, confirm the subscribers, share classes, voting rights, board size, and initial paid-in capital. Notarize the Articles of Incorporation and the founding directors consents if required by the bank, Investment Commission, or the registered agent. Open a temporary capital contribution account in Taiwan, remit all subscribed funds by wire or SWIFT, and obtain a bank remittance receipt. Engage an independent certified public accountant to perform capital verification and issue the capital verification report. Execute the organizers statutory declaration and the first directors declaration of lawful compliance before submitting to the registry.
required_dossiers: Share subscription agreement and subscribers list
Notarized consent to act of each director
Bank capital remittance and receipt certificate
Foreign investment approval letter if obtained
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the capital verification is queried, supplement wire-chain evidence and bank statements or correct the currency conversion calculation; if notarization is suspended, cure the defective signature or foreign legalization and re-notarize; if the capital does not arrive within the subscription period, pass a shareholders resolution extending the payment date and amend the capital verification report accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Formal Company Registration and Issuance of Registration Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan, via the One-Stop Company Registration online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for company registration online or at the MOEA counter within the statutory filing period, attaching the name reservation approval, notarized Articles of Incorporation, founding meeting minutes, CPA capital verification report, foreign investment approval, registered office consent, and directors identity documents. The examining officer checks the proposed business scope, capital, legal purpose, directorship qualifications, and foreign investment compliance. After approval, the registrar issues the unified company registration certificate and company identification number. Preserve the electronic MOEA registration record and synchronize the approved business items with the tax authority for subsequent tax and business registration.
required_dossiers: Photocopies of directors and shareholders identity documents
Registered office address consent and proof of address
Company seal specimen and registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or suspension, submit a supplemental legal brief and corrected schedules within 21 days; if the application is rejected, amend the affected provisions and refile; if the decision is adverse after reconsideration, administratively appeal to the Ministry of Economic Affairs and, if necessary, seek judicial review within the statutory limitation period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Banking and Foreign Exchange Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Regional National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan; Taiwan commercial banks; Taiwan Central Bank foreign-exchange reporting system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After MOEA registration, complete tax and business registration with the competent National Taxation Bureau to obtain the tax identification number and the business registration certificate. Open operating bank accounts in Taiwan, including syndicated loan and foreign-currency wire accounts, and file board resolutions, signatory cards, corporate seal specimens, and director identification with the bank. Register the inbound foreign capital investment with the Taiwan Central Bank foreign exchange data filing system and obtain the foreign investment remittance certification from the bank. Arrange bank-level AML/KYC due diligence, including source of wealth, beneficial ownership, sanctions screening, and intended transaction profile for the leveraged buyout SPV.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation and certificate of registration
AML/KYC questionnaire, beneficial ownership form, and bank references
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, reconcile the MOEA registration data and provide supporting certificates; if a bank refuses account opening due to AML or enhanced due diligence concerns, supplement the SPV structure, funding chain, and transaction flow or apply through another permitted institution; if the Central Bank foreign-exchange filing is incomplete, instruct the bank to file corrective remittance codes and resubmit the foreign investment return.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Certificates, Statutory Registers and Beneficial Ownership Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of CN_JV_LTD; company secretary or professional corporate agent; MOEA commercial registration for beneficial ownership disclosure
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After company registration, prepare share certificates bearing the required statutory signatures, maintain the shareholders register, directors register, and corporate seal ledger, and deliver these statutory books to the registered office. Prepare and file the beneficial ownership information report with MOEA under the AML/CFT regime, including the natural-person beneficial owners of the private equity syndicate, and update the report within the prescribed period whenever ownership changes. Adopt board operating procedures, conflicts-of-interest policy, and delegated authority table. Ensure all formation documents, notarized instruments, capital evidence, and board resolutions are indexed and preserved by the corporate secretary or registered agent.
required_dossiers: Beneficial ownership report form to MOEA
Board minutes with powers of attorney
Registered agent acceptance and custody receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the beneficial ownership filing is rejected, correct the identity and control mapping and resubmit; if share certificates are defective, pass a board resolution to cancel and reissue; if registers are incomplete or lost, reconstruct them with affidavits and supporting transaction documents, and engage a licensed professional corporate secretary to certify the restoration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable for a passive ISIC 6499 private equity buyout SPV; if physical manufacturing, assembly, chemical, or warehousing operations are later added, the Industrial Development Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan, would be the coordinating industrial licensing authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operation is being conducted; the SPV holds passive equity interests and execute buyout loan transactions only.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable; would be the Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan, Taiwan, if physical facilities are later established.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no EIA required because the SPV has no physical construction, manufacturing plant, waste discharge source, or regulated stationary emissions unit.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. If future Taiwan operations are added, the applicable quantitative thresholds under Taiwan environmental law would include effluent pH between 6 and 9, chemical oxygen demand not exceeding 100 mg/L, biochemical oxygen demand not exceeding 30 mg/L, suspended solids not exceeding 30 mg/L, volatile organic compound emissions as limited by the Taiwan Air Pollution Control Act plant-specific permitting standards, and hazardous waste handling under the Taiwan Waste Management Act with registered manifesting and treatment approval.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable to a purely financial SPV. If a physical registered office or service office is occupied, the premises must hold a current fire safety inspection certificate under the Taiwan Fire Services Act and Building Act, and any occupied workplace must comply with the Taiwan Occupational Safety and Health Act, including exit marking, emergency response plans, electrical safety, and general workplace hygiene inspection.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (R.O.C.) through its Department of Taxation and the competent local National Taxation Bureau for the entity's registered place of business; electronic portals are the E-Tax Portal (https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw) and the E-Invoice Integration Service Platform (https://www.einvoice.nat.gov.tw).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity must appoint a tax representative in Taiwan and file the statutory tax-registration application with the competent National Taxation Bureau before commencing activity. The applicant must submit: (i) the foreign certificate of incorporation or equivalent constitutional instrument; (ii) a resolution approving the Taiwan business/registration; (iii) the appointed tax representative's letter of appointment, passport, and resident certificate, together with the representative's Unified Business Number/TIN; (iv) evidence of the Taiwan physical place of business (lease or service-agreement contract) or, for a pure offshore electronic-service supply, a cross-border e-commerce VAT registration declaration; and (v) the standardised application form used by the National Taxation Bureau for tax registration. For non-resident cross-border e-commerce operators, the registration is made under the simplified tax-registration regime for foreign electronic-service suppliers; after documentary review, the National Taxation Bureau issues an 8-digit Unified Business Number (TIN) and tax-registration certificate. If the foreign entity has no fixed place and no trade presence in Taiwan, no general VAT registration is required; VAT withholding obligations may apply on Taiwan-source service payments by the Taiwan payer.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not operate a US-style check-the-box election, does not provide pass-through classification for limited-company SPVs, and has no domestic hybrid-mismatch entity election. A foreign entity with a Taiwan branch is taxed at entity level on Taiwan-source profit; a Taiwan-incorporated JV is taxed as a resident entity. Fiscal-year selection is administrative rather than an entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act; commonly referred to as Taiwan Business Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NT$480,000 per year for non-resident electronic-services suppliers; NT$80,000 per month of goods sales or NT$40,000 per month of services sales as the statutory taxability threshold for domestic/onshore small business. A domestic entity with a fixed place of business must register before commencement of business irrespective of projected turnover where output is not otherwise exempt.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic Uniform Invoices are mandatory for VAT-registered enterprises that choose to use e-invoices and for designated categories. The issuer must connect via the MOF E-Invoice Integration Service Platform Turnkey service (machine-to-machine API) to upload invoice data; B2C e-invoices are typically transmitted within 48 hours of issuance, and B2B data is filed through the same channel. Taiwan does not operate a real-time continuous-transaction-control (CTC) fiscal clearance model; the anti-fraud mechanism is a platform-validated electronic invoice number, QR code, and random anti-fraud selection code. Paper uniform invoices remain lawful where e-invoicing is not mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods qualify for the 0% VAT rate when they are actually exported from Taiwan: the goods must be sold in the export trade, shipped out of the customs territory, and supported by a customs export declaration. Qualifying offshore services (including electronic and digital services) are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident for use or consumption outside Taiwan and paid in foreign exchange. The zero-rated status must be proven by contemporaneous export, logistics, contractual, and foreign-exchange repatriation records at the time of the VAT periodic filing; input VAT associated with zero-rated exports may be reclaimed through the VAT refund mechanism after statutory scrutiny.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration as released by the Taiwan Customs Administration
Commercial Invoice and Uniform Invoice/Packing List
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill/Courier Receipt proving actual export movement
Export sales contract or purchase order containing the price and incoterms
Bank foreign-exchange settlement certificate or inbound SWIFT/payment record evidencing receipt of the export consideration from the foreign buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau cross-checks export zero-rating against customs release records, bank foreign-exchange receipts, and e-invoice data. If any required export document is missing, the foreign-exchange consideration is not repatriated within the statutory 180-day period, or the export is found to be simulated or misdeclared, the tax authority retrospectively reclassifies the supply as taxable, assesses 5% VAT on the sales consideration, imposes overdue tax interest and late penalties, and may impose a punitive fine of up to five times the evaded tax pursuant to the Business Tax Act. Falsifying export documents or deliberately obtaining a zero-rate can trigger criminal tax-evasion liability under the Tax Collection Act and Criminal Code, including imprisonment; the filing position may also be reopened for audit beyond the ordinary assessment period if fraud is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC) as the onshore Taiwan FX authority, together with the People's Bank of China (PBOC) and its State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) for any PRC-controlled capital flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Taiwan's FX regime is an open but managed system. Current-account transactions such as trade payments, service fees, royalties, dividends, and interest can be converted and remitted through CBC-designated foreign exchange banks without central bank approval, provided the remitter submits underlying invoice/contract documentation and a foreign exchange settlement or declaration form. Capital-account flows, including equity injection, fund redemption, M&A consideration, investor loans, and profit repatriation outside standardized exemptions, require CBC filing; where a People's Republic of China entity is an investor, the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) must grant cross-strait investment approval before the inbound remittance is accepted. The New Taiwan Dollar is not fully internationalized and remains subject to rate management by the CBC, which also monitors settlement through the domestic banking units. There is no statutory surrender duty on export receipts; a Taiwan corporation may keep export proceeds in foreign currency or sell them, subject to transaction-backed declarations. Profit remittance is permissible only after audited financial statements, tax filing, withholding settlement, the original capital-verification report, and the bank's CBC remittance coding are in place. For the PRC-side partner, SAFE outbound investment registration and the bank's capital account filing are mandatory before funds can leave China, and any mismatch with Taiwan's MOEA/CBC requirements can freeze the entire clearing chain.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For a Taiwan-domiciled exporter, the CBC requires export proceeds to be collected through an authorized designated bank within the statutory period, generally 120 days after shipment unless an extension is approved; no mandatory conversion ratio applies because Taiwan does not impose a surrender regime. The receipt must be reported on the FX settlement/declaration form and may be retained in USD or another permitted currency, or converted into New Taiwan Dollars at market rate. If the Chinese joint-venture partner books export revenue on the PRC side, SAFE's current-account rules require repatriation of those proceeds into China within the applicable filing window and settlement through a designated bank; any offshore retention must be individually approved by SAFE. The SPV itself is not an exporter unless it takes title to goods, in which case these rules bind its treasury.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (USD/NTD) and Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account (USD/NTD) and Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account (TWD/USD) and Syndicated Loan Wire Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Pure fintech EMIs have low viability in Taiwan. Taiwan's Banking Act and CBC regulations reserve multi-currency corporate lending, foreign exchange, and cross-border clearing for licensed banks and designated financial institutions; an unlicensed EMI cannot open a legally effective corporate account or connect directly to CBC settlement systems. Digital-only banks in Taiwan hold commercial banking licenses and may be used, but they do not eliminate the underlying KYC or the requirement for a physical or video-verified board mandate. Offshore EMIs such as Wise, Revolut, or Airwallex should not be used as the primary treasury rail for the SPV because they lack Taiwan deposit-taking authority and any partner-bank arrangement reintroduces the same Tier-1-bank compliance gate.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Taiwan banks generally require the statutory responsible person of the SPV to appear at the opening branch or a designated branch for a face-to-face interview; this can be done through an approved online video KYC with the bank's digital onboarding module, but the director must sign a corporate account mandate and provide a valid passport and company seal. If the board sits outside Taiwan, banks accept a notarized power of attorney authenticated by the local Taipei Economic and Cultural Office or competent notary, plus a Taiwan resident authorized signatory; however, for a medium-risk PE SPV, the bank's AML committee usually insists on a live interview with the ultimate beneficial owner and at least one deal partner before activation, making remote consular-only opening impractical.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multilayered cross-border ownership with nominee or trust vehicles concealing the ultimate PE investors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the SPV's certificate of incorporation and current articles; full ownership chain from each ultimate individual through every holding company; notarized passports and proof of residential address for all UBOs; trust deed/foundation constitution where applicable; shareholder register with transfers; signed source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations; and a fund formation or side-letter package evidencing where each capital commitment originates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The SPV has no operating business, no employees, and its buyout activity creates significant unexplained cash movements and capital calls.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Investment committee approval and latest fund prospectus; executed limited partnership agreement or shareholders' agreement; acquisition agreement with seller and target names; committed financing letters with terms and maturity; detailed capital call and distribution waterfall; board resolution authorizing the banking relationship; full year projection of cash flows and debt service; and an independent asset valuation for the acquisition target.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-strait sanction, PEP, and dual-use trade exposure arising from the PRC shareholder and Taiwan-target supply chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fresh OFAC, UN, EU, UK, HKMA, and Taiwan CBC sanctions screening output for all shareholders, counterparties, and target companies; PEP declarations completed by every beneficial owner; export-control classification/end-use certificate for any goods involved; list of all intermediaries in the transaction chain; and a group anti-money-laundering and anti-bribery compliance manual.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity investment from a PRC entity into a Taiwan PE vehicle lacks both cross-strait investment approval and SAFE ODI registration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Taiwan MOEA Investment Commission approval or official filing receipt; CBC inward remittance declaration with the exact FX purpose code; SAFE ODI certificate and local bank registration record from the PRC-side investor; board resolutions and corporate chop authentication certificate; CPA capital verification report; and an escrow instruction letter signed by both investors and the Taiwan receiving bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity and shareholder-loan proceeds must be transmitted by SWIFT MT103 from the investor's bank to the SPV's capital escrow account at the chosen Tier-1 Taiwan bank. The wire must name the SPV exactly, cite the MOEA Investment Commission approval number or filing reference, state the CBC foreign exchange purpose code for direct investment, and identify the ultimate remitter to avoid incoming-remittance repricing. For a PRC investor, the PRC bank must also cite SAFE ODI/filing and cross-border capital account registration before releasing the RMB or foreign currency. On receipt, the Taiwan bank will file the inward remittance declaration with the CBC, freeze the funds in the capital escrow bucket, and require a Taiwan-licensed CPA to issue a capital verification report tied to the purchase price and the exact NTD/USD exchange rate. The escrow may be released only after the CPA verification, the bank's enhanced KYC committee sign-off, and the corporate authorized-signatory instruction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: All trade and operating disbursements should clear through the Tier-1 bank's domestic banking unit or offshore banking unit. Direct cash payments must use SWIFT MT103 with an underlying invoice, contract, or disbursement instruction and the applicable CBC trade purpose code. For physical goods, use an irrevocable commercial letter of credit transmitted by SWIFT MT700/MT707 or, for smaller counterparties without LC appetite, a documentary collection (D/P or D/A) against full set of shipping documents. The SPV may also use a Bank Payment Obligation (BPO) under the Uniform Rules for Bank Payment Obligations to reduce documentary friction with the syndicated lender. RMB payments to PRC suppliers should be routed through the CBC-authorized RMB clearing channel or via the bank's cross-border RMB settlement service, but in all cases the disbursement must have a matching import/export declaration or M&A payment schedule to survive bank compliance review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forwards in TWD/USD, TWD/CNY, and USD/CNY up to the amount of documented trade, loan, or dividend exposure, with a maximum tenor of 12 months and no cash-settlement delivery unless an underlying invoice or debt repayment is proven.

FX swaps and cross-currency swaps through the Tier-1 bank's DBU/OBU, used strictly to align the currency base of the syndicated loan with the SPV's equity and receivable portfolio; swaps must be back-to-back with the funding leg and cannot create a leveraged speculative FX position.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in TWD or CNY may be executed only through a CBC-approved offshore branch or OBU, and only when onshore delivery is legally or commercially impossible; the SPV must submit a board-approved hedging policy, monthly mark-to-market report, and underlying exposure schedule to the bank, and speculative NDF trading is strictly prohibited.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting resolution acknowledging the balance sheet, profit and loss statement, business report, earnings appropriation or loss recovery proposal, and subsequent registration of any registrable resolutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting of the JV; Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) for registrable changes; Investment Commission, MOEA for foreign-investment-related changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the December 31 fiscal-year end, i.e. no later than June 30; registrable resolutions must be filed with MOEA within 15 days after the shareholders' meeting or adoption date, and within 30 days after Investment Commission approval when the change affects the foreign-investment permit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible directors may be fined TWD 10,000 to TWD 50,000 per violation for failure to prepare or submit annual financial statements to shareholders; continuing non-compliance with a six-month suspension of business may trigger MOEA administrative dissolution and company-register strike-off under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual company information and beneficial shareholding declaration of directors, supervisors, managers, and shareholders holding 10% or more of the JV share capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) via the electronic company information registration platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between March 1 and May 31; any in-year change in directors, supervisors, managers, or 10%-plus shareholders must additionally be filed within 15 days after the effective date of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file, late filing, or false filing attracts an administrative fine of TWD 50,000 to TWD 500,000 per event under the relevant Company Act enforcement provisions; MOEA may order rectification and continuously impose fines until correction; persistent delinquency combined with inactive operations may lead to administrative strike-off under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-seeking enterprise income tax return and unappropriated earnings tax report, with audited financial statements attached if the audit threshold is met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (competent district tax office for the JV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 of the year immediately following the calendar tax year; if May 31 falls on a weekend or national holiday, the deadline is postponed to the next working day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is penalized under Income Tax Act Article 108 at 10% of the assessable underpayment, with a minimum penalty of TWD 3,000 if no tax is due; false or underreported income carries an additional penalty of 20% of the tax amount under Article 110; underpayment interest accrues monthly at the statutory one-year postal time-deposit rate; protracted delinquency plus cessation of business for over six months may trigger MOEA administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added and non-value-added business tax return covering monthly or quarterly sales, purchases, and tax remittance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (competent district tax office for the JV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly filers: by the 15th day of the following month; quarterly filers: by the 15th day of the month following the end of the quarter; all deadlines extend to the next working day if the statutory date falls on a holiday
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: For late filing, a penalty of 1% of the tax due applies for every two-day delay up to a maximum of 10%; if no tax is due, the late-filing penalty is TWD 1,500; omission or false under-declaration may additionally attract a penalty of 1% to 2% of the under-declared tax amount per month, capped at 10%, and may expose the entity to tax collection beyond the normal five-year limitation period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding income statement and employee exemption/remuneration statement for salaries, dividends, fees, and other income paid by the JV
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (competent district tax office for the JV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before January 31 of the following calendar year; withholdings from non-residents must be remitted within 10 days of the payment date, with final annual reconciliation due by the January 31 deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or underreporting withholding statements can result in fines under the Income Tax Act of up to 20% of the underwithheld or unremitted tax amount, plus monthly underpayment interest; continuous non-compliance may be treated as a serious corporate-governance defect by MOEA and may contribute to administrative dissolution if the company is inactive.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit by a licensed Taiwan CPA is required: (1) for public companies and companies whose shares are listed or traded on the Taiwan Stock Exchange or Taipei Exchange under the Securities and Exchange Act; (2) for non-public companies whose paid-in capital exceeds TWD 30 million (approximately USD 1.0 million) under Company Act Article 20, as designated by MOEA; (3) for financial institutions, banks, insurers, securities firms, financial holding companies, and other FSC-supervised enterprises regardless of capital size; (4) for foreign-invested companies, including Sino-foreign equity joint ventures, when the Investment Commission approval or foreign investment permit expressly conditions the annual report on certified CPA financial statements; and (5) for enterprises applying for a Blue Return or certain tax incentives that require a CPA-attested financial report. Taiwan law does not impose a standalone annual revenue or headcount trigger for audit of a private non-public special purpose vehicle; the controlling quantitative trigger for this PE SPV is the balance-sheet paid-in-capital threshold of TWD 30 million.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The governing framework is the Business Entity Accounting Act, the Regulations on the Preparation of Financial Reports by Public Companies for listed public issuers, and either IFRS Accounting Standards as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission (TIFRS) for public companies and large enterprises or Taiwan Enterprise Entity Accounting Standards (Taiwan EAS) for qualifying non-public enterprises. A private PE buyout SPV is ordinarily Small and Medium Enterprise or non-public and will prepare statutory financial statements under Taiwan EAS; however, the foreign parent partner may require IFRS-compliant accounts for consolidation. Accounting vouchers must be retained for at least five years and accounting books and financial statements for at least ten years under Article 26 of the Business Entity Accounting Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act Article 22-1, the JV must annually confirm with MOEA, through the electronic company registration system, the identity and shareholding percentage of every shareholder holding 10% or more of the share capital, together with the names of directors, supervisors, and managers. The annual confirmation window is March 1 through May 31. Any share transfer or other change that causes a person to meet, exceed, or fall below the 10% beneficial shareholding threshold must be reported to MOEA within 15 days after the effective change; where the transfer is an approved foreign-investment transfer, the related registration must be completed with MOEA within 30 days of the Investment Commission permission or the transfer closing, whichever is later. The annual confirmation is not a substitute for the 15-day event-driven filing.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 12,000 per annum, depending on portfolio complexity, intercompany positions, and whether IFRS consolidation schedules are required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% (Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax); an additional 5% unappropriated retained-earnings tax applies if profits are not distributed.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket SPV tax holiday. Preferential treatment available only for statutory investment tax credits (R&D, green energy, cultural assets) and for the retained-earnings surcharge which is waived for current-year distributions. Foreign tax credits apply for taxes paid in the P.R.C.
